one_line: Sixth Sikh Guru who embodied miri-piri by uniting spiritual leadership with armed defense of the community.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s to early 40s, athletic and grounded, with a calm but battle-ready build.
appearance.face: Oval face with a warm medium-brown Punjab complexion, high cheekbones, neatly kept full black beard with slight taper, straight nose, thick brows, and a steady, compassionate gaze; default expression is serene but resolute, like a calm commander ready to act.
appearance.hair: Long black hair tied neatly in a topknot beneath a medium-height rounded turban; turban is deep navy blue with a subtle wrap, a narrow white band peeking at the base, and a small steel chakar (quoit) tucked on the left side.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate early 17th-century Sikh warrior-saint attire: a knee-length deep navy-blue jama (flared, long-sleeved Mughal-style tunic) of sturdy cotton with simple stitched panels, worn over a light cream cotton chadar-like under-robe; a wide saffron cotton kamarband (waist sash) wrapped twice and knotted on the left, with the sword belts emerging from it; loose white cotton churidar-style trousers gathered at the ankles; simple but sturdy brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes; over the torso, a fitted matte steel char-aina–style breastplate and backplate (no fantasy spikes, just clean riveted plates) strapped with brown leather; minimal jewellery limited to a small steel kara (bangle) on the right wrist and a modest steel ring on one finger, evoking practicality and humility.
appearance.signature: Two curved steel talwar swords symbolizing miri-piri, each in a plain leather scabbard with simple steel fittings: the ‘miri’ sword worn slightly higher on the left, the ‘piri’ sword lower on the right, both suspended from brown leather belts emerging from the saffron kamarband, hilts wrapped in dark leather with understated steel pommels.

ref_desc: Guru Hargobind is a mid-30s athletic Sikh man with a warm brown complexion, full black beard, navy turban with a steel chakar, deep navy jama over cream garments, saffron kamarband, steel breastplate, white churidar, and twin steel talwar swords for miri-piri at his waist.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Guru Hargobind as a dignified early 17th-century Sikh warrior-saint: a mid-30s athletic man with a warm medium-brown complexion, oval face, high cheekbones, and a neatly kept full black beard, his expression serene yet resolute; his long black hair is tied in a topknot under a medium-height rounded deep navy turban with subtle wrapping, a narrow white band at the base, and a small steel chakar tucked on the left side. Dress him in a knee-length deep navy-blue cotton jama with long sleeves and flared skirt, worn over a light cream under-robe, a wide saffron cotton kamarband wrapped twice and knotted on the left, and loose white cotton churidar-style trousers gathered at the ankles, finished with simple brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes. Over his torso, show a realistic matte steel char-aina–style breastplate and backplate with clean riveted plates and brown leather straps, with minimal adornment; add a small steel kara on his right wrist and a modest steel ring on one finger. At his waist, show two curved steel talwar swords symbolizing miri-piri, each in a plain brown leather scabbard with simple steel fittings, the ‘miri’ sword worn higher on the left and the ‘piri’ sword lower on the right, hilts wrapped in dark leather; ensure the dominant colours are deep navy blue, saffron orange, cream, white, and steel grey, and present him in a neutral stance from multiple angles so his face, turban, armour, garments, and twin swords are all clearly visible for consistent redraws.
